paper_title: Energy transfer by feebly interacting particles in supernovae: the trapping regime
notes: Paper presents NEW constraints on axion-photon coupling from supernova energy deposition, extending previous work to the 'trapping regime' where diffusive heat transport dominates over ballistic transport at large couplings. Figure 3 shows exclusion limits for two progenitor scenarios: Rprog = 5×10^13 cm (0.1 B explosion) and Rprog = 3×10^12 cm (1 B explosion). The main novel result is that at sufficiently large couplings (small mean free paths), the energy deposited saturates and decreases as g_aγ^-2 due to diffusive transport, rather than continuing to increase as predicted by previous ballistic-only calculations. The paper derives constraints from SN 1987A X/γ-ray observations and low-energy supernovae (LESNe). Data points extracted from Figure 3 represent approximate bounds at the edges of the constrained region: lower coupling limit ~1e-12 GeV^-1 and upper coupling limit ~1e-4 GeV^-1, spanning axion masses from ~1 MeV to ~1 GeV. The exact numerical values from Figure 3 are difficult to read precisely, so confidence is moderate (0.75). The paper also discusses implications for dark photons and sterile neutrinos but focuses primarily on axion-photon coupling.
